newsitem.title: USA: Ex-U.S. Navy worker accused of spying for S. Korea.
newsitem.headline: Ex-U.S. Navy worker accused of spying for S. Korea.

text.p: Former U.S. Navy intelligence employee Robert Kim has been indicted on three espionage charges for passing classified information to South Korean last year, the Justice Department said on Thursday.
It said a federal grand jury in Alexandria, Virginia charged that Kim gave or attempted to give seven documents relating to the U.S. national defence to a South Korean official.

Kim, 56, who had been a civilian computer specialist with the Navy since 1978, had access to secret and top-secret information during his military career. The Korean-born Kim became a U.S. citizen in 1974.

According to the indictment, Kim delivered and mailed the classified documents to the Korean official's residence. The documents contained information about the Korean peninsula and a computerized maritime tracking system.
The espionage charges carry a maximum sentence of life in prison without parole.

Kim was arrested in September at a diplomatic reception at Fort Myer, Virginia and charged with passing classified information to South Korean Navy Capt. Baek Dong-Il, who worked at the South Korean embassy.
Kim has remained in jail without bail since his arrest. He was dismissed from the Navy after his arrest.

An arraignment for Kim, when he is expected to enter a plea to the charges, has been set for March 31. The indictment was handed up by the grand jury on Wednesday and made available by the Justice Department on Thursday.
